ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the upper left of the figure there is H3N: with a lone pair of electrons, and its curved arrow points to the indicated H; this H is connected to the carbon on the left, and the carbon on the left is also connected to an R group and to the carbon on the right. The carbon on the right is connected to OH and NH2. The figure also draws one curved arrow from the C-H bond toward the C-C bond between the two carbons, and another curved arrow indicates that the C-O bond electrons move toward O. Then reason: According to pushing electrons with the arrows, ammonia first abstracts this H; the original C-H bond electrons are used to form a C=C double bond between the two adjacent carbons; at the same time the C-O bond breaks, the electrons go to oxygen, and OH leaves. The remaining organic fragment is R-CH=C(NH2)H; written as SMILES according to the shown alkene configuration, it is [*]/C=C(N)\[H].

raw_record.question_text: An 'arrow-pushing' diagram is a common type of chemical image used to illustrate electron flow in mechanistic steps. Please choose the SMILES expression for the molecules(state) after the electron has been relocated, as depicted in the image. <image_1>

method.method_draft: First describe the image: identify the substrate as R-CH-C(NH2)(OH) with the left carbon bearing the indicated H, and note the three curved arrows from ammonia to H, from the C-H bond toward the C-C bond, and from the C-O bond to O. Apply the arrows in order: remove the H as a proton, use the former C-H electron pair to make a double bond between the two carbons, and break the C-O bond so OH leaves. The remaining molecule is R-CH=C(NH2)H with the drawn E/Z orientation corresponding to [*]/C=C(N)\[H].
method.CoT_raw: 先描述图像：图中左上方有带孤对电子的 H3N:，其弯箭头指向标出的 H；该 H 连在左侧碳上，左侧碳还连有 R 基并与右侧碳相连。右侧碳连有 OH 和 NH2。图中还画出一支弯箭头从 C-H 键指向两个碳之间的 C-C 键，另一支弯箭头表示 C-O 键电子移向 O。再推理：按箭头推动电子，氨先夺取该 H；原 C-H 键电子用于在相邻两个碳之间形成 C=C 双键；同时 C-O 键断裂，电子给到氧，OH 离去。剩余有机片段为 R-CH=C(NH2)H；按照图示烯烃构型写成 SMILES 为 [*]/C=C(N)\[H]。

Encode the resulting substituted alkene R-CH=C(NH2)-H in SMILES with R as [*] and the depicted stereochemistry, yielding [*]/C=C(N)\[H].
